goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: Verification passes, and encryption, replay, feedback bounds, TTL filtering, conflict history, and workspace isolation are materially implemented. The authority chain is not ready. Ontology promotion trusts caller-supplied gate booleans and caller-supplied claim objects rather than resolving current canonical authority and computing compatibility/evaluation itself; the improve worker never automatically promotes shadows and records extractor proposals before verification. Its E2E fixture supplies synthetic episodes with inline payloads rather than consuming reopened canonical working-store evidence. Enrichment authority duplicates graph checks but omits provenance revalidation, while source tombstones are not propagated. Session-close consolidation processes every workspace episode, not the closed session. These gaps block KG-AC10 and the claimed end-to-end milestone.

worker_package.objective: Repair T006 as one authority-complete ontology/improve vertical slice. Make ontology promotion non-forgeable: the registry must accept canonical support claim IDs, resolve their current graph authority itself, reject tombstoned/revoked/expired/provenance-invalid support, compute structural, backward-compatibility, scope, collision, and versioned retrieval-evaluation gates through trusted deterministic code or hash-bound evaluator artifacts, and never trust caller-supplied claim bodies or pass/fail booleans. After independently verified admission, the improve worker may create an admission/provenance-bound shadow proposal and must automatically reevaluate eligible shadows after each admitted claim; default-three independent authoritative support plus every computed gate promotes add-only changes to a new immutable version without a manual promote call. Unverified extraction must create neither graph truth nor ontology proposals; destructive changes remain quarantined. Consume real encrypted canonical working-store episodes through a source-owned monotonic cursor and independently reopened/hash-verified evidence, including late-arrival coverage. Centralize claim authorization in the graph boundary so enrichments use the same current provenance, admission, TTL, tombstone, and revocation decision as recall. Propagate canonical source tombstones/revocations to graph authority before enrichment rebuild. Consolidate only episodes belonging to a canonically closed session, keep degraded notifications retryable, and prove idempotent completion within 120 seconds. Add deterministic explicit-alias resolution evidence while preserving incompatible homonyms. Correctly map IM-AC02 to session consolidation and IM-AC03 to bounded non-authoritative feedback. Preserve disabled-by-default behavior and do not implement router, MCP/API recall, deployment, or live services.

stop_if: Promotion still accepts caller-supplied gate verdicts, evaluation scores without a hash-bound trusted evaluator result, or caller-supplied claim bodies as authority.
The registry cannot resolve current canonical support claims and reject tombstoned, revoked, expired, provenance-invalid, duplicate-authority, or cross-workspace support at promotion time.
Automatic shadow reevaluation/promotion requires a manual promote call, or an unverified extraction can persist an ontology proposal.
A real canonical episode cannot be paired with independently reopened evidence whose content hash and workspace/session scope are verified before extraction.
The high-watermark remains based only on observed_at and can permanently skip late-arriving canonical episodes.
Enrichment authorization diverges from graph recall authorization or source tombstones/revocations can leave an authoritative enrichment visible.
A session-close notification is not backed by canonical close state, processes another session, permanently caches a degraded result, or cannot meet the deterministic 120-second acceptance bound.
Explicit alias resolution can merge incompatible homonyms without independently verified binding evidence.
Any required change falls outside allowed_files or requires router, MCP/API recall, deployment, live credentials, network access, or a real user vault.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.
